title: Lima for a First Visit: Pick Your Neighborhoods
dek: A coastal base, an old-city outing and space for a very good lunch.
body:
## Start with a base
Miraflores and Barranco make useful starting points for comparing stays. Miraflores puts the coastal malecón into the conversation; Barranco suits a visit shaped around neighborhood streets and the Puente de los Suspiros. Choose the exact address after deciding which outings matter most to you.

## Give each district its own time
Plan a historic-center morning around Plaza Mayor. On another outing, choose Huaca Pucllana in Miraflores or Museo Larco in Pueblo Libre. These are separate destinations within the city, so leave transfer space instead of treating them as stops on one continuous walk.

## A gentle two-day outline
Spend the first day with Miraflores and Barranco, pausing along the coast if the weather suits. Use day two for the historic center and a separate museum afternoon. If that feels too busy, keep just one major museum and spend the extra time over lunch.

## Before you commit
Check museum access and current visitor information, then save the places you actually want to see. The starter itinerary is an editable outline: its sequence is not a verified walking route. Leave meals flexible around the neighborhood you are already enjoying.

title: Lima: Market Ingredients, Museum Lunches and Craft
dek: A food-and-design day with room to make your own discoveries.
body:
## Begin with ingredients
Mercado de Surquillo No. 1 offers a different lens on Lima from a restaurant reservation. Look at the produce, ask questions when a stallholder has time, and ask permission before photographing people. A market visit can be a short browse; it need not become a shopping list or a fixed meal.

## Make lunch part of the outing
Museo Larco has a café-restaurant in its garden setting. If the museum is already part of your plan, compare the current menu and availability before arranging lunch. Keep admission and dining arrangements separate, and avoid booking a cross-city table immediately after a timed visit.

## Browse with a question
The museum store offers books, jewelry and textiles. Ask about materials and makers rather than assuming every item has the same origin. For a deeper design read, open the Meche Correa story in this city’s Journal; its editorial background is not a promise of current boutique hours or stock.

## Keep the day flexible
Choose either a market-led morning or a museum-led afternoon as your anchor. Save the relevant places and add them to your trip, leaving transport and a comfortable meal pause between districts.

title: Meche Correa in Lima: Peru’s Living Archive of Color and Craft
dek: A joyful wardrobe of memory, craft and unapologetic Peruvian color.
body:
Fashion Strolls · Lima, Peru

Meche Correa in Lima

A joyful wardrobe of memory, craft and unapologetic Peruvian color.

In Lima, where Pacific mist softens the city’s palette, Meche Correa’s work arrives like a celebration. Embroidery, woven texture and saturated color turn clothing into a living archive—one that carries Peru’s regional traditions forward without freezing them in the past.

A self-taught designer and artist with more than 35 years of work, Correa has built her house around cultural identity and direct collaboration with artisan communities across Peru. Named an Ambassador of Marca Perú in 2011, she approaches fashion as both expression and preservation.

Peruvian memory, made contemporary

Correa’s aesthetic is instantly recognizable: graphic florals, hand-worked details, dramatic accessories and silhouettes that feel festive rather than precious. The point is not to reproduce traditional dress. It is to let ancestral techniques and regional visual languages enter a modern wardrobe with confidence.

For the traveler, her pieces offer something rare—a sense of place that does not depend on a souvenir logo. A richly embroidered jacket can transform neutral trousers; a woven bag brings Lima energy to a simple linen dress.

The hero jacketLet embroidery carry the look. Add black, cream or deep denim and keep jewelry sculptural.

The woven accentA compact bag or belt adds craft and color without competing with a travel capsule.

The evening shiftTrade flat sandals for a polished heel and add one luminous earring—no full change required.

How to shop the story in Lima

Approach the collection slowly and ask about technique, material and community collaboration. Because availability and appointments can change, confirm current shopping details directly through the official Meche Correa site before visiting.

Jet Set LatAM styling note: Pack statement pieces flat with tissue, repeat their colors elsewhere only once, and let craftsmanship stay central. Continue the Peruvian fashion conversation with our feature on Mozhdeh Matin in Lima.

A wardrobe with emotional geography

What makes Correa compelling is the belief that heritage can remain alive only when it keeps moving. Her work connects art, identity and social responsibility, yet never loses pleasure. These are clothes for women who want their wardrobe to feel collected, personal and gloriously awake.

The final word

Meche Correa makes fashion feel like a map drawn in color. In Lima, her work offers a sophisticated reminder: the most modern thing a traveler can wear may be a story carried forward with care.

title: Montevideo for First-Timers: Old City, Open Water
dek: A compact city break that leaves room for the Rambla.
body:
## Begin between two chapters
Plaza Independencia is a useful orientation point between Centro and Ciudad Vieja. Let the first outing be about the historic city: an architecture pause, a look at the Teatro Solís schedule and a wander along pedestrian Sarandí. Check the theater’s current access rather than assuming a tour will be available when you arrive.

## Choose your base around your evenings
Compare a Centro or Ciudad Vieja address if historic sights lead your plans. Consider Pocitos or the Parque Rodó area when waterfront time matters more. These are different neighborhood choices, so check the exact stay location and the transfers your itinerary would require.

## Leave room by the water
The Rambla is best treated as time outside rather than a distance target. Pick a manageable section around Pocitos and allow yourself to turn back whenever you like. Wind or rain can shift that outing to another day.

## A first-visit rhythm
Use one day for Ciudad Vieja and a market lunch; use another for green space and the waterfront. Save your essential places first, then edit the two-day starter to match your arrival time and energy.

title: Montevideo: Markets, Parrilla and a Little Shopping
dek: Choose a market, browse slowly and keep lunch at the center of the day.
body:
## A meal at the port market
Mercado del Puerto is associated with parrilla dining in Ciudad Vieja. Walk through, read the current menus and choose the table that suits your appetite. The market is the recommendation here; no individual stall is being presented as a tested favorite.

## A different market outing
Mercado Agrícola de Montevideo is in Goes, away from the port-market setting. Treat it as a separate visit for food and browsing rather than a second stop on an assumed walking route. If you only have two days, choose the market that best fits the rest of your plans.

## Shopping between sights
Pedestrian Sarandí makes browsing part of an old-city wander. Punta Carretas Shopping offers an indoor alternative in a former prison complex, useful when you want a more conventional shopping stop. Neither requires turning the whole afternoon into an errand.

## What to ask
For a gift or wearable piece, ask about origin, material and care. Check prices and return terms with the seller. Keep purchases and editorial recommendations separate: this guide does not attach an endorsement to every business inside a market.

title: Two Slow Days in Montevideo
dek: Historic streets first; park and waterfront time next.
body:
## Day one: the historic city
Begin at Plaza Independencia, then shape the morning around Ciudad Vieja. A Teatro Solís visit can be the anchor if the current schedule works; otherwise enjoy the architecture and continue toward Sarandí. Leave lunch flexible at Mercado del Puerto rather than overbooking the day.

## Day two: green space and water
Choose Parque Rodó for an outdoor interval and make a separate waterfront outing around Pocitos. Punta Carretas Shopping is an optional indoor pause, not a required detour. Check transfers between neighborhoods and the weather before deciding the order.

## If you have less time
Keep one historic-city stop and one stretch of Rambla. Dropping a stop is often more rewarding than rushing through every item. The editable starter gives you a beginning, not a completion challenge.

## Make it yours
Save the places that appeal, copy the starter into Plan and add personal notes. A market lunch can move with your appetite. A theater booking should lead the schedule if you make one. There are no claimed walking durations between these stops: check pedestrian directions separately if you intend to connect them on foot.

title: Panama City: Choose a Base, Then Choose an Outing
dek: Casco, canal and causeway are three different reasons to stay.
body:
## Give Casco its own morning
Casco Antiguo is the historic-city chapter: plazas, architecture and museums. Start around Plaza de la Independencia and choose a museum that interests you. The Museo del Canal focuses on canal history; Museo de la Mola introduces a very different cultural story.

## Compare stays by location
An old-city address suits a visit centered on Casco. A stay elsewhere in the modern city may suit other plans, but check the exact neighborhood and the transfers it creates. A skyline view alone will not tell you how your days will work.

## Plan the canal separately
Miraflores requires deliberate visitor-center and transport planning. Confirm current access before setting aside that part of the day. Amador and the Biomuseo make another outing, with waterfront time if conditions suit.

## Keep a two-day visit selective
Use one day for Casco and a food pause. On the other, choose your canal visit and decide whether you still want Amador afterward. The published two-day Journal guide offers more detail, while the starter itinerary lets you save an editable outline. Leave space for weather and transfers instead of assuming a continuous walk connects the city.

title: Panama City: Seafood, Molas and Thoughtful Browsing
dek: Learn about a craft before shopping; leave room for a seafood pause.
body:
## Start with the story
Museo de la Mola offers an introduction to Guna mola art. Let that learning shape the questions you ask when browsing: who made the piece, what technique was used and how should it be cared for? A museum visit and a purchase are separate decisions.

## Browse deliberately
Panama’s tourism board includes a Mercado de Artesanías among city outings. Confirm its current location before setting off. This guide does not publish an unverified shop pin, a numbered walking circuit or a claim that every stall sells the same kind of work.

## Make space for lunch
Mercado de Mariscos is a seafood-market option to consider around a city outing. Compare current vendors, menus and preparation choices for yourself. It is a food area, not a tested endorsement of an individual counter.

## Build a useful city day
Choose one cultural anchor, one browsing pause and a meal that fits your route. Save the places first, then decide their order in Plan. For what to wear, use the wardrobe companion to think through your city day; current shop stock, weather and restaurant expectations should guide the final choices.

title: Two Days in Panama City: Casco Viejo, the Canal and Amador
dek: Give the old town, the canal and the waterfront their own space—then decide whether the next chapter is beach or highland.
body:
Give the old town, the canal and the waterfront their own space—then decide whether the next chapter is beach or highland.

At a Glance

  • Day one: Casco Viejo
  • Day two anchor: Miraflores Visitor Center
  • Flexible addition: Amador Causeway
  • Next chapter: Bocas del Toro or Boquete

Make two days feel like two days

Panama City is more rewarding when the old town, the canal and the waterfront are treated as distinct outings. This is a suggested two-day sequence, not a timetable: change the order around current opening information, weather and your arrival.

Start with the Panama destination hub. If you land late, count the following morning as the start of the plan rather than compressing the whole first day into a few hours. Choose a stay for its actual location and the evening you want, not only for the skyline in its photographs.

Day one: let Casco Viejo be the main event

Build the first day around Casco Viejo, also called Casco Antiguo. Panama Tourism describes a historic district of plazas, museums, viewpoints and shops in its official old-town guide. Pick a small number of indoor stops and leave room between them.

Our suggestion is a first walk for orientation, a meal without a rushed departure and one museum or cultural stop that genuinely interests you. If you prefer a guided introduction, compare what the tour covers and where it finishes. Save the rest of the neighborhood for an unhurried return rather than trying to complete every listing.

Day two: build around the canal visit

Make Miraflores your main reservation or planning anchor. The official Miraflores Visitor Center page explains the viewing experience and provides current admission information. Use that page for opening details and tickets rather than relying on a copied price or an old timetable.

Check what your chosen ticket or tour includes, whether transport is included, and how you will return. Do not treat a guide’s sample schedule as a promise of ship movements. Leave space around the visit so that one delayed journey does not unravel the whole day.

Amador: an optional waterfront chapter

The Amador Causeway offers a different perspective: skyline and canal-entrance views, with places to walk, cycle and pause. Panama Tourism also points visitors toward the Biomuseo and Punta Culebra Nature Center in this area.

Add Amador if the day still has room. Choose one activity or a waterfront break instead of promising yourself every attraction. Our Panama City cycling guide is a companion for planning a ride; confirm the route and rental arrangements you intend to use. On a short visit, dropping an optional stop is often better than racing through it.

Before reserving the pieces

  • Accommodation: compare the precise address with your evening plans.
  • Canal outing: distinguish admission from transport and any additional guided services.
  • City tour: check the meeting point, duration, walking involved and cancellation terms.
  • Departure day: leave room for the airport journey rather than attaching a final attraction to a tight flight connection.

The trip planner helps arrange the sequence. Keep confirmations and meeting points together in the app so the plan is usable after you close the research tabs.

Choose one extension, then give it time

For an island chapter, read the Bocas del Toro beach guide. For highland interests, start with our Boquete and Panama highlands story. These are onward-trip choices, not additions to the same two city days.

The Playa Venao guide offers a Pacific-coast alternative. If you are visiting around celebrations, consult Panama’s holiday traditions as background and verify the dates of any event separately. Return to the Panama hub to keep the whole route in view.

Make the plan yours

Once you have chosen your base, compare the exact location, room details and cancellation terms.

title: San José, Costa Rica: A Capital Worth a City Day
dek: Theater, coffee and collections before the next leg of your trip.
body:
## Begin in Centro
The National Theatre is a natural orientation point for a first visit. Choose a tour or performance only after checking the current schedule, then leave time for coffee nearby. The city’s museums give this part of a Costa Rica journey a different rhythm from a beach or forest stay.

## Pick one collection
The Pre-Columbian Gold Museum, Museo del Jade and Museo Nacional offer different starting points. One unhurried museum visit usually fits a short stop better than racing between all three. Look at current exhibitions before choosing.

## Compare neighborhoods
Centro suits a plan led by the theater and collections. Barrio Amón adds an architecture-focused wander; Barrio Escalante is worth considering for a separate food outing. Check the exact address when comparing stays and allow for your onward transport.

## Keep travel days realistic
Do not treat an airport transfer or a journey to the coast as invisible time. If you arrive late, save the major museum for the following day. Use the city’s editable starter as a framework, keeping coffee, lunch and an open interval around the one visit you most want to make.

title: San José: Coffee, Market Browsing and Museum Finds
dek: A small food-and-craft circuit, with no need to rush the coffee.
body:
## Pause at the theater
Alma de Café is the National Theatre’s café, offering Costa Rican coffee and pastries. Make it a pause around your cultural visit, then check the current menu and service arrangements directly. It can be the enjoyable interval between sights rather than another appointment.

## Follow your curiosity at Mercado Central
The market offers food, coffee and browsing under one roof. Look around before deciding where to eat or what to buy. Ask about preparation, ingredients and packaging, especially if you plan to take anything home.

## A more focused shop stop
The Central Bank Museums Shop provides a browsing opportunity beside the collections. Ask about the maker, origin and materials of a piece. A thoughtful purchase does not have to become a long shopping afternoon.

## Keep the evening separate
B​​arrio Escalante is another food-focused part of the city to consider if you want a dedicated dining outing. Choose a current venue and arrange your transport before committing. Save your daytime places into Plan, but keep meal choices flexible: this guide adds ideas, not automatic restaurant assignments.

title: Two Days in San José: Culture with Breathing Room
dek: One central-city day, then history and a green-space afternoon.
body:
## Day one: theater and coffee
Start with the National Theatre area and a pause at Alma de Café. Choose the Gold Museum if its current exhibitions fit your interests, then leave a flexible interval for Mercado Central. The starter keeps these ideas together without assigning a fixed lunch vendor.

## Day two: choose your pace
Consider Museo Nacional for the morning. Later, make a separate outing west to Museo de Arte Costarricense and La Sabana. If two museums feel like too much, choose one and give the park or a neighborhood wander more time.

## Adjust for your journey
A two-day outline is not a requirement to spend two complete days sightseeing. Remove stops around flights, onward transfers or a late arrival. Confirm opening days before deciding which museum belongs on which day.

## Save the useful parts
Copy the starter into Plan, add personal notes and save the places you want to return to. Suggested day order is editorial, not a verified pedestrian route; arrange transport between districts as needed. Keep an indoor alternative for outdoor plans and make the final sequence fit the forecast and your energy.

title: Florianópolis: A First-Timer’s Guide to Brazil’s Island Capital
dek: Find your corner of Floripa: lagoon life, Atlantic surf and long seafood lunches.
body:
Find your corner of Floripa: lagoon life, Atlantic surf and long seafood lunches.

Florianópolis — “Floripa” to Brazilians — is a state capital that happens to sit mostly on an island. Santa Catarina Island has dozens of beaches, a big saltwater lagoon, forested hills and fishing villages settled by Azorean immigrants, all within an hour or so of each other. It is where Brazilians go for surf, seafood and long summer nights.

First Trip at a Glance

  • Choose a base: Lagoa, Jurerê or Campeche
  • Beach mood: Atlantic surf; calmer northern shores
  • Peak season: December–March
  • Getting around: A car helps with spread-out beaches

Where to stay

  • Lagoa da Conceição — the island’s social center, around the lagoon: restaurants, bars and easy access to both east- and south-coast beaches.
  • Jurerê Internacional — the polished north, with calm water, beach clubs and a glossier scene.
  • Campeche and the south — quieter and wilder, with long beaches and a more village feel.

Find a stay that fits your base and pace.

Compare Florianópolis hotels ↗

Opens Booking.com in a new tab. Enter your destination and dates to search; availability varies.

The beaches

The east coast faces the open Atlantic, so beaches like Joaquina and Praia Mole draw surfers — Joaquina also backs onto sand dunes where you can try sandboarding. The north is calmer and warmer for swimming. In the south, trails lead to more remote coves. Our Florianópolis beach guide goes deeper.

What to eat

Florianópolis is known for its oysters, farmed in the calm bays on the island’s western side — the old Azorean village of Santo Antônio de Lisboa is a lovely place to try them at sunset. Otherwise, think fresh fish, shrimp and long beach lunches.

When to go

Summer, from December to March, is peak season: hot, lively and busy, with higher prices. The shoulder months either side are quieter and still warm enough for the beach, while winter (June to August) is cool and calm.

Getting there and around

Florianópolis has its own international airport with frequent flights from São Paulo and Rio. A car makes it much easier to explore the island’s spread-out beaches.

title: Where to Stay in Florianópolis: Lagoa, Jurerê or Campeche?
dek: Pick the part of the island that fits the days you actually want to have.
body:
Pick the part of the island that fits the days you actually want to have.

Start with your beach plans

Where to stay in Florianópolis is less about finding one “best” neighborhood than deciding what you want nearby. Lagoa da Conceição suits a social, varied trip; Jurerê Internacional puts the polished northern beach scene first; Campeche and the south favor a quieter, wilder setting.

Before opening a hotel map, choose your two must-do beach days and the kind of evening you want. A lovely room on the opposite side of the island can mean spending more of your trip getting between places. Our Florianópolis first-timer’s guide covers the wider picture.

Lagoa da Conceição: for variety

The lagoon is the island’s social center, with restaurants, bars and access to the east- and south-coast beaches. Make this your starting point if you want several kinds of days: Atlantic surf, a dune outing and an evening around the lagoon.

Joaquina and Praia Mole draw surfers; Joaquina also has dunes for sandboarding. Think of Lagoa as a base for exploring, rather than assuming a lagoon address gives you an ocean beach outside the door. Check the exact location of a prospective stay against the beach you expect to visit most.

Jurerê Internacional: for a beach-led stay

Choose Jurerê when your ideal trip revolves around the polished north: calm-water beaches, beach clubs and a glossier atmosphere. It makes sense to prioritize the setting you want to return to each afternoon, especially if you prefer fewer excursions.

The trade-off is a different emphasis from the east coast’s surf scene or the south’s quieter coves. If those dominate your wish list, compare the practical journeys before committing. Visit Brasil’s destination overview also distinguishes Jurerê’s lively scene from the island’s other beach areas.

Campeche and the south: for a slower rhythm

Campeche and the southern part of the island offer long beaches and a more village-like feel. Put them first if the beach itself is the reason for coming, and a quieter setting matters more than a full evening circuit.

Build a few spacious days instead of using a southern stay as a launchpad for every northern beach. The Florianópolis beach guide is a useful companion when choosing which shores deserve your time.

Before you book

  • Map the actual address. Compare it with your main beach and dinner plans, not just the neighborhood name.
  • Decide on transport. A car makes the island’s spread-out beaches easier to explore. If you plan to rent one, ask the property about parking before booking.
  • Choose one base first. For a short trip, our recommendation is to settle into one area and make selective outings, rather than packing up repeatedly.
  • Match the season to the mood. December–March is the busy summer period; winter, June–August, is cooler and calmer.

Once you have chosen your part of the island, compare stays by exact location and cancellation terms.

title: Florianópolis: Market Lunches and Island Craft
dek: Give Centro a day of its own between beach outings.
body:
## Start in the center
The Mercado Público is a natural food stop for a Centro outing. Look at the current seafood menus and choose a table that suits the day. Leave the meal unhurried instead of stacking several distant beaches around it.

## Browse the customs house
Casa da Alfândega houses the Galeria do Artesanato. Make time to look closely at materials and techniques, and ask about the maker and origin of a piece. Craft shopping works best as a conversation, not a hunt for a predetermined bargain.

## Add a different island chapter
Santo Antônio de Lisboa offers a separate village outing, with Praça Roldão da Rocha Pires as an orientation point. Compare that option with your beach priorities and allow for transport. It does not need to be squeezed into the same afternoon as every Centro stop.

## A balanced short stay
Use one day for central history, craft and market food, then choose Lagoa and one beach for another. Read the city’s first-timer and where-to-stay stories before deciding your base. Save the starter, remove anything that makes the day feel crowded, and leave room for changing beach conditions.
